entries.what_happened: Three manuscripts in the family; two bear directly on this problem. (a) “Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2” (FM2) claims in Theorem 1.1 that every continuous, irreducible, odd two-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ, unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, is isomorphic to a Tate twist of the 2-adic representation of a classical cuspidal eigenform. Its abstract says this resolves the odd, regular two-dimensional Fontaine–Mazur conjecture over ℚ at 2, including all residual representations. The argument has three stages: potential pro-modularity over a solvable totally real field F of even degree, split completely at 2, obtained by connectedness and patching from a modular seed (Theorem thm:potential-promodularity); production of a locally algebraic vector with the target eigensystem, using ordinary families and Thorne's Theorem D in the reducible local case and the local Langlands correspondence in the absolutely irreducible local case; and descent from a regular algebraic Hilbert cusp form over F, obtained by Jacquet–Langlands from a definite quaternion algebra, to ℚ by cyclic descent with a finite-character twist. The introduction adds that the geometric realization of modular representations gives the geometric-origin conclusion in this setting; the body does not argue that. (b) “Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two” (UPM2) claims, with no de Rham or residual hypothesis, that every continuous odd absolutely irreducible 2-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in the full completed two-adic Hecke algebra 𝕋₂(N) at some odd level N: there is a continuous ℤ₂-algebra map λ: 𝕋₂(N) → O_E with λ(T_ℓ) = tr r(Frob_ℓ) and λ(ℓS_ℓ) = det r(Frob_ℓ). It states that it does not assert classical modularity. Its proof places r in a fixed-determinant trace family, finds an auxiliary regular de Rham point x, applies FM2's Theorem 1.1 to x to get classicality, and then uses the dimension theorem of (c) and Newton–Thorne's adjoint Selmer vanishing to show the original point lies on Hecke support (conclusion.tex, proof of Theorem main). (c) “The Dimension of the Two-Adic Hecke Algebra at Odd Level” (DHA) claims that for every odd N every irreducible component of Spec 𝕋₂(N) has Krull dimension exactly 4, the p = 2 case of Emerton's dimension conjecture. It makes no claim about Galois modularity; it bears on this problem only as an input to UPM2.
entries.delivers: For the list's Fontaine–Mazur problem, FM2 proves, at p = 2 only, the odd, regular, two-dimensional case over ℚ: an odd, irreducible, two-dimensional 2-adic representation, de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and unramified outside finitely many primes, is modular up to Tate twist (a classical cuspidal eigenform). The residual representation is unrestricted, and scalar and reducible residual cases are included. This corresponds to the list's part (3), restricted to dimension two, odd, regular, and at 2, and to the modularity half of part (2) in that case. The list's part (3) matches FM2's statement, apart from the prime, which is 2 only. The list's part (2) uses ‘potentially semistable at p’ and FM2 uses ‘de Rham at 2’; the text passes from de Rham to potentially semistable by citing Berger (lemma dense-Thorne-points). The geometric-origin conclusion of part (1) is asserted in one sentence of the introduction and not proved in the body. FM2's introduction says that, together with odd-prime results discussed there (Pan 2022; Zhang 2025 for p = 3), the theorem gives the modularity conclusion ‘at every prime’. Those odd-prime results are other papers, and this family proves only p = 2. UPM2 delivers less: occurrence in a completed Hecke algebra for every odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation, with no Hodge–Tate or de Rham condition. It delivers no classical modularity for any representation, so it does not give the conjecture's conclusion. DHA delivers no Galois-theoretic conclusion. The manuscripts claim to resolve the odd regular two-dimensional case over ℚ at 2, not the conjecture as a whole. None of them addresses the even case, the equal-Hodge–Tate-weight case, totally real base fields, the unramified-everywhere / finite-image statement, the group-theoretic reading, or the tame variant.
entries.remains: If the claims hold, the following stay open for the list's problem: (i) every prime other than 2 within this family, since the every-prime statement depends on external odd-prime papers; (ii) the even two-dimensional case, where the conjecture predicts nonexistence; (iii) the equal-Hodge–Tate-weight (irregular) case for classical modularity, where UPM2 gives only occurrence; (iv) general dimension, general number fields, and the geometric-origin conclusion beyond the one-sentence claim; (v) totally real base fields (list item 6); (vi) the unramified-everywhere / finite-image statement (item 7), the group-theoretic reading (item 8), and the tame variant (item 9); (vii) classical modularity of the representations that UPM2 shows occur in the completed Hecke algebra, which UPM2 says it does not assert.
entries.direction: proves a case: odd, regular, two-dimensional over ℚ at p = 2, classical modularity up to Tate twist; plus a weaker occurrence-only pro-modularity result for all odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional cases at 2
entries.conditional_on: FM2's Theorem 1.1 relies on cited results it does not prove. Thorne, ‘Towards the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture for GL₂’ (arXiv:2608.07186v1, a 2026 preprint), Theorem D, is used in the reducible local branch to make dense ordinary points modular (lemma dense-Thorne-points); this is the main external dependency. Other inputs are BLGGT 2014 Theorem 2.1.1 (Galois representations for Hilbert cusp forms at 2), Colmez 2010 and Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas 2014 (local p-adic Langlands at 2), Berger 2002 (de Rham implies potentially semistable), Jacquet–Langlands and Arthur–Clozel (base change and descent), and Billerey–Menares 2016 for the existence of cuspidal lifts in the reducible-residue connectedness step, which the manuscript says it re-proves in detail. UPM2 is conditional on FM2 (Theorem 1.1 applied to its auxiliary point, and the curve and connectedness arguments it takes from FM2), on DHA (its dimension-four theorem), on Newton–Thorne 2023 Theorem 5.4 as specialised to GL₂/ℚ, and on Allen 2016 Lemma 1.1.3. Its introduction also cites Thorne's Theorem D as supplying an essential set of classical points, but I found no body section that cites Thorne. DHA is conditional on Emerton's Corollary 2.28 (the lower bound of dimension 4) and on Newton–Thorne Theorem 5.4 as specialised to GL₂/ℚ at p = 2.
entries.doubts: FM2: (1) The geometric-origin conclusion is asserted in a single sentence of the introduction with no argument in the body, which ends at ‘classical cuspidal eigenform’. (2) The reducible local branch rests on Thorne's 2026 preprint (Theorem D), which is cited as the source of modularity for its dense ordinary points. (3) The every-prime claim in the introduction depends on odd-prime results outside the family. (4) The virtually solvable case (Lemma solvable-reduction) is argued in about sixty lines: the imaginary quadratic subcase is handled by citing theta series and Jacquet–Langlands, and the real quadratic subcase by a unit-theorem argument. (5) I read the statements and key steps of the classicality, connectedness and preliminaries sections; I did not read the patching, deformation, completed_forms or fields sections in full, and checked them only by grep for hedging language. I did not check the proofs in detail. UPM2: (1) Its main theorem is occurrence, not classicality, so it inherits every dependency on FM2 and DHA. (2) Thorne's Theorem D is named in the introduction as an essential input, but I found no body section citing it. (3) The marked-line, transverse-chart and Selmer-loss construction for the scalar and reducible-residue branches is described in the introduction; I read the introduction and the regular-point section (lines 1–60, 330–404) in full and grepped family.tex, diagonal.tex and hecke.tex for citations and hedging words only, so those branches are checked only at the level of the introduction. DHA: (1) The lower bound (every component has dimension at least 4) is quoted from Emerton's Corollary 2.28 ‘with p = 2’. The text says its own determinant argument supplies the p = 2 justification for Emerton's Theorem 2.7, which had an odd-prime restriction; whether that repair also covers Corollary 2.28 is asserted, not separately shown. (2) The Selmer-vanishing input, Newton–Thorne Theorem 5.4 specialised to GL₂/ℚ, is stated to include p = 2 and a CM condition. The cited paper's title, ‘Adjoint Selmer groups of automorphic Galois representations of unitary type’, is about unitary-type groups, so the specialisation carries real weight in the argument.
